title: Young Japanese Have Worse Diets than Older Japanese
paragraphs: Many people think that Japanese food is very healthy. But a new study says that many young people in Japan do not eat well.

A group of researchers from the University of Tokyo studied the diets of people in Japan. The news was reported in October 2026. The researchers found that people in their teens and early 20s had the worst diets. Middle-aged and older people had better diets.

Why do young people eat worse? The researchers think that it may be because their lives change a lot at this age. For example, many young people start university or a new job. These changes may affect the way they eat every day.

The study found that some habits were linked to poor diets. People who did not eat breakfast often had worse diets. People who smoked also had worse diets. The researchers also found that a person's income and education were related to the quality of their diet.

Other information shows a similar result. According to a survey by Japan's health ministry, adults in Japan ate an average of 256 grams of vegetables a day in 2023. This was the lowest amount since 2001. People in their 20s ate the fewest vegetables. In general, the older people were, the more vegetables they ate.
So, what can young people in Japan do? Eating breakfast every day and eating more vegetables may be good first steps.
